name: Beibingyang (北冰洋) soda
blurb: Beijing's polar-bear orange soda in glass bottles, gone in the late 1990s, back in 2011
title: What Is Beibingyang (北冰洋)? Beijing's Polar Bear Soda
description: Beibingyang (北冰洋, "Arctic Ocean") is Beijing's classic polar bear orange soda, made from the 1950s, lost after a 1994 Pepsi venture and revived in 2011.
answer: Beibingyang ("Arctic Ocean") is a Beijing soda brand best known for its orange soda in glass bottles with a polar bear on the label. It traces back to a 1936 ice factory and started making sodas in the 1950s, becoming the soda of Beijing childhoods. After a 1994 joint venture with Pepsi it was sidelined and disappeared by the late 1990s. The brand was recovered in 2007 and relaunched on 1 November 2011, and it is still sold today.

body: Picture a thick glass bottle of bright orange, strongly fizzy soda with a white polar bear logo. Early versions used real fruit and often had a little sediment at the bottom; besides orange there were sour plum and lemon flavours. You usually drank it right at the shop and handed the bottle back, since bottles were reused. The 2011 relaunch kept that system, with a 1-yuan deposit per bottle.

sections.h: Why it vanished and came back
body: In the 1990s several old Chinese soda brands entered joint ventures with global cola companies. In Beibingyang's case, output fell year by year after the Pepsi deal until it stopped altogether and the old factory site was sold. Once the restriction ran out, the revived company relaunched it in 2011, swapping saccharin and artificial colouring for orange concentrate and orange oil and redrawing the polar bear. It is widely available in Beijing and sold elsewhere in China.

faq.a: Yes. It relaunched in November 2011 and is sold in glass bottles and cans, most widely in Beijing.
